### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/metadata-fs`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **11** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-core/src/repository.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via FileSystemRepository (symbol, a top-level class), SysMetadataRepository (symbol, a top-level class))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-core/src/repository.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **13** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ba57588665fd846eb95b682b3660f52a697370a9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `50c4601d4e8e193ad185ec6b05f5ebb6b7e21063` — the merge of head `046c425d62db1c00fade07cde87f632c1bd7f899` into base `ba57588665fd846eb95b682b3660f52a697370a9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 50c4601d4e8e193ad185ec6b05f5ebb6b7e21063 && git checkout 50c4601d4e8e193ad185ec6b05f5ebb6b7e21063
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ba57588665fd846eb95b682b3660f52a697370a9 046c425d62db1c00fade07cde87f632c1bd7f899 && git checkout -B drift-repro ba57588665fd846eb95b682b3660f52a697370a9 && git merge --no-ff 046c425d62db1c00fade07cde87f632c1bd7f899

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ba57588665fd846eb95b682b3660f52a697370a9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ba57588665fd846eb95b682b3660f52a697370a9` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## REWORK (seat review, narrow) — PR #21814 at head `071959e91e`

`domain:engine#1` · `session_017ErfyP2Rx7XWHJA27QjyUi` · read at 2026-10-05T04:54Z. The os-dev report is on #21790 (5988341325). Judged against GitHub and the branch, not against the report.

**The fix itself reads right, and nothing in the mechanism is asked to change.**
- `canonicalize(value, type?)` and `hashSpec(value, type?)` keep `object.fields`' insertion order through a one-row table. Every other map, and every key inside a field definition, stays key-order independent. A call with no type is byte-identical to before.
- `SysMetadataRepository.put`'s no-op check re-hashes the stored body under the current rule, only for a type with an ordered map. A skipped write returns the stored stamp, so upgrading raises no 409 (H4).
- The census answers H1 and H2. The two reverse-verification legs went red exactly on the order half and on the stamp comparison.
- Both open questions are answered **A** (accept the FS provenance default as recorded; locale maps stay out), on the reasons the report gives. Both are already stated in the changesets and the PR body.

**One defect: the `Clause-②` line.**
- The clause asks one question (`scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`): does this card relax an accept set or **widen the public surface**?
- This diff widens `@objectstack/metadata-core`'s published surface. `orderedMapKeys` is a new export through `index.ts` (`export * from './canonicalize.js'`), and `canonicalize` and `hashSpec` take a new parameter. The metadata-core changeset says so itself: "two exports widen".
- So the line is `Clause-②: yes`, not `no`. The seat's claim predicted `no` before the diff existed; the PR states what the diff does.
- **Asked:**
  1. Line 2 of the PR body becomes `Clause-②: yes`.
  2. The changesets' `Clause-②:` lines agree with it.
  3. Each moved package carries the level `check-changeset-no-major` requires under `yes`, measured with the corrected body.
- **Asked, one measurement:** state that every caller of `hashSpec(…, ref.type)` in the three repositories receives the canonical singular type. `orderedMapKeys('objects')` is `[]`, so a plural spelling would silently hash order-blind. Name where the spelling is folded before `put`.
- **Then:** with `Clause-②: yes`, a contract review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` is owed before landing. The seat runs it on the corrected head.

Recorded, not filed, as the report states: the `DatabaseLoader` second checksum vocabulary (no caller in `packages/*/src`), and `dry-run-hash-compat.ts`'s `checksum_drift` arm firing on new stamps (an offline probe).

## ACCEPT (seat review) — PR #21814 at head `046c425d62` · contract review owed before landing

`domain:engine#1` · `session_017ErfyP2Rx7XWHJA27QjyUi` · read at 2026-10-05T05:53Z. This follows the seat's narrow REWORK 5988361846 and two patch rounds. The dev's follow-ups are on #21790.

- **REWORK resolved:**
  - Line 2 of the PR body and all three changesets read `Clause-②: yes`. `orderedMapKeys` is a new export of `@objectstack/metadata-core`, and `canonicalize`/`hashSpec` take a new parameter, so the public surface widens.
  - Levels: metadata-core `minor`, metadata-protocol and metadata-fs `patch`. `check-changeset-no-major` over the corrected body exits 0, and its level axis reads `yes` with metadata-core at `minor`. `check-adr-0087-registration` exits 0.
- **The type-folding measurement:**
  - `saveMetaItem`, publish and `rollbackMetaItem` fold the type to the canonical singular before `put`.
  - `revertCommit`'s restore limb passes a stored manifest-plural type (`objects`) to `put`, so the ordered-`fields` rule does not apply to such a legacy row. Measured with a restored probe.
  - The seat answered A: this PR records it in its Acceptance notes, and the closure is its own ruling, filed as #21821.
- **Docs (patch round 2):** `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`'s hash paragraph now says what the code does:
  - keys sort, except in the maps the spec declares ordered (today `object.fields`);
  - `put()` short-circuits on an unchanged body;
  - a row written before this release keeps its stored hash until its content next changes.

  All 41 gates derived for that path exit 0, `check:doc-authoring` included.
- **Mechanism, unchanged since the review at `071959e91e`:**
  - `object.fields` keeps its insertion order in the canonical form.
  - Every other map, and every key inside a field definition, stays key-order independent. A call with no type is byte-identical to before.
  - `SysMetadataRepository.put` re-hashes the stored body under the current rule for an ordered type, and a skipped write returns the stored stamp. So no spurious 409 follows an upgrade.
- **Both open questions:** answered A in the REWORK (the FS provenance default is recorded; locale maps stay out).
- **CI on `046c425d62`:** 42 check runs, 38 success, 4 skipped, 0 failed. The failed type-check and Test Core runs earlier in the timeline were on the superseded heads `071959e91e` and `6fe110968c`, cancelled by the newer push.
- **Labels:** `needs:contract-review` is hung on this PR in this act. `Clause-②: yes` makes the review owed. The seat runs it at its tier on this head, posts the record, and only then lands.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `046c425d62db1c00fade07cde87f632c1bd7f899`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #21790 (body, comments 5987334318, 5987515805, 5988341325, 5988409457, 5988464990, 5988540414), PR #21814 (body, 14-file list, net diff against the merge-base `18c7dfd2e6`, which is the PR's base sha), and the 46 check-runs on the head. Line numbers below are at the head unless marked `main`. Every seat conclusion on the thread was set aside, as the brief asks.

Gate verdicts on the head: every completed check-run is `success` or `skipped`; none failed. `Check Changeset` ran three times on this head (111625285701, 111625466899, and 111634383656 after the label write) and all three are `success`. Type Check (workspace, source gates, consumer gates, debt ledger), Lint and Repo Gates, Build Core, Build Docs, Test Core 1 to 6, Dogfood Regression Gate 1 to 3, Dogfood Verify CLI, Temporal Conformance, Spec property liveness, Governed Surface Queue Guard, and the four claim and part-of gates are all `success`. The Docs Drift Check (PR comment 5988314939) states CI read the merge of this head into `ba57588665`, so the gates judged the head on a newer main than the head itself merges.

### ① Derived judgments

Public surface of `@objectstack/metadata-core` (all reached through `packages/metadata-core/src/index.ts:11`, `export * from './canonicalize.js'`):

- `canonicalize(value, type?)` takes a new optional parameter (`canonicalize.ts:131`). Widening. Declared in the changeset (`.changeset/21790-metadata-core-ordered-fields-hash.md:9`). Right.
- `hashSpec(value, type?)` takes the same parameter (`canonicalize.ts:226`). Widening. Declared (same changeset, line 9). Right.
- `orderedMapKeys(type?)` is a new export (`canonicalize.ts:120-122`). Widening. Declared (line 10). Right.
- Omitting `type` is the old rule byte for byte: `orderedMapKeys(undefined)` answers the frozen empty list (`canonicalize.ts:83`, `:120-122`), so `normalise` sorts every map as before (`:206`). Pinned at `test/canonicalize.test.ts` ("with no type, a reorder of `fields` hashes equal" and the empty-spec fixture). Right.
- The table has one row, `object` to `fields` (`canonicalize.ts:110-111`), and is a `Map`, so `orderedMapKeys('constructor')` is empty rather than an inherited function (`:107-108`, pinned). Right.
- The row is grounded in spec prose, not renderer behaviour: `packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts:1080-1084` (`main`, "the in-group display order equals the traversal order of `ObjectSchema.fields`", ungrouped fields "preserving their field declaration order"), `:2090-2093` (`main`), `field.zod.ts:90` (`main`, "Insertion order = display order"), `display-name.ts:50-52` (`main`). The triage direction 5987334318 ("no explicit order key") is honoured: no key is added. Right.
- Only the root position receives `orderedChildren`; every deeper position receives none (`canonicalize.ts:159-163`, `:195`, `:208`). So the keys around `fields` and the keys inside each field definition still sort. Pinned (the H5 block, plus a 200-run property). Right.
- Insertion order equals `Object.keys` order only when no key is integer-like. The field-key grammar is `/^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$/` (`object.zod.ts:2076-2079`, `main`), which admits no such key, so guarantees 5 and 7 hold as the docblock argues (`canonicalize.ts:54-58`); pinned as properties under `object`. Right.
- `MetadataItemSchema.hash` only changes its `describe` text (`types.ts:100`); the regex is unchanged, so no accept set moves. Right. One residue: `types.ts:94-95` still says "Equal hashes imply equal specs", which is false on one legacy edge the PR body discloses (see ③, item 10). Doc-level, not blocking.
- Repository contract invariant 4 is restated as `item.hash === hashSpec(item.body, item.ref.type)` (`repository.ts:24-29`, `contract-suite.ts:15`, `:207`, `:230-235`, `:270`). An external `MetadataRepository` that still hashes type-blind breaks the invariant only for `object` bodies with unsorted `fields`; every in-tree implementation is updated (below). Right, and the restatement is the honest one.

`@objectstack/metadata-protocol` (`sys-metadata-repository.ts`):

- `put` hashes as `ref.type` (`:539`). The optimistic lock still compares the caller's token with the stored stamp (`:614-616`), never a re-derivation, so an upgrade raises no 409. Right.
- The no-op short-circuit asks `storedBodyUnchanged` (`:630`), which for a type with an ordered map re-hashes the stored bytes under the current rule (`:1998-2013`); for every other type it stays a stamp comparison (`:2004`). This is the only repository that persists stamps across the rule change, so it is the only one that needed a content comparison. `InMemoryRepository` holds no legacy stamps (`in-memory-repository.ts:105-108`) and `FileSystemRepository` re-derives its heads at boot (`metadata-fs/src/repository.ts:519`), so their stamp comparisons are right.
- A skipped write answers `item.hash`, the stored stamp (`:630-632`), so a receipt token over a legacy row is the one the next `If-Match` must send. Pinned at the repository (`sys-metadata-repository.contract.test.ts:690-700`) and end to end (the dogfood file, "the receipt's token is honoured by If-Match"). Right.
- `rowToItem` re-derives only a null checksum, as its type (`:1955`). Right.
- The designer's door reaches `put` under the canonical singular spelling: `saveMetaItem` folds at `protocol.ts:19452` and puts at `:19628`; publish folds at `:20762` and promotes at `:20924`; rollback folds at `:24388` and `:24395` and restores at `:24454`. `revertCommit` builds its ref from the stored type (`:23876`) behind a guard that passes manifest plurals (`:23840`), so a legacy `objects` row restores order-blind. That residue is disclosed in the PR body and carried by #21821. Right.
- No other production caller of `hashSpec` or `canonicalize` exists in `packages/*/src` (the `canonicalize` at `plugin-auth/src/member-role-canonical.ts:245` is a local arrow function, not the import). The ETag and `If-Match` paths the dev cites do not re-derive the content hash. Right.

`@objectstack/metadata-fs` (`repository.ts`): all four hash sites pass `ref.type` (`:263`, `:363`, `:519`, `:1006`). A version-pinned `get` with a pre-change token answers null (`:264`) and the JSONL log's pre-change hashes no longer match (`findMetaForHash`), which the changeset discloses as the provenance fallback (`.changeset/21790-metadata-fs-ordered-fields-hash.md:9`). Right.

Docs: `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx:149` now states the rule the code implements (keys sort except in spec-declared ordered maps, `put()` short-circuits on an unchanged body, a pre-release row keeps its stamp as its version token). I found no other hand-written page stating sorted-key hashing. `docs/adr/0008-metadata-repository-and-change-log.md:183` still reads "sha256 of `canonicalize(body)`"; that is a governed ADR's original design text, not a page this PR may edit in passing. Right.

Done-when of the card: "a pure reorder is hashed as a change" holds (`canonicalize.ts:206-208`, pinned), and "a dogfood test reorders, publishes, reloads and reads the new order" holds: `packages/qa/dogfood/test/object-designer-field-reorder.dogfood.test.ts` saves a draft reorder, publishes, reads `GET /meta/object/:name` twice, and reads the stored row, on the showcase over real HTTP. Triage's second pin, an unordered map still hashing equal under a key swap, is the H5 block of `test/canonicalize.test.ts`. Both pins are on the head, and Test Core and the Dogfood Regression Gate are green on it.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/metadata-core`: `minor` (`.changeset/21790-metadata-core-ordered-fields-hash.md:2`). Right: a new exported symbol on an index and two widened signatures is "a purely additive widening of a published package's public surface", which takes at least `minor`; a `fix(` that widens an index is `minor` (`.github/workflows/pr-automation.yml:754-760`).
- `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`: `patch` (`.changeset/21790-metadata-protocol-ordered-fields-hash.md:2`). Right: no exported symbol, key, value, payload or error code changes; `storedBodyUnchanged` is private (`sys-metadata-repository.ts:1998`).
- `@objectstack/metadata-fs`: `patch` (`.changeset/21790-metadata-fs-ordered-fields-hash.md:2`). Right: a behaviour fix with no surface change, with its residue stated in the body.
- `skip-changeset` is absent and would be wrong: three released packages publish.
- Nothing is removed or renamed, so no BREAKING banner and no ADR-0087 marker is owed (`AGENTS.md:1078-1089`).
- `Clause-②: yes`. The PR body's line 2 reads `Clause-②: yes`, and each changeset mirrors it (line 7 of each), which is where the gate reads it (`AGENTS.md:1087-1088`). The public surface of `metadata-core` widens, so `yes` is the true answer; the claim's `no` (5987515805) was a prediction made before the diff existed, and the dev corrected it on the diff (5988464990). No direction arm is written; the arm is optional (`AGENTS.md:1075-1077`). `yes` takes at least `minor` on one moved package, which `metadata-core` satisfies; the level axis passed three times on the head (`Check Changeset` 111625285701, 111625466899 and 111634383656).
- No governed path is in the 14-file list, so no Tier H or Tier S record is owed by path; this record answers the `Clause-②: yes` declaration and the `needs:contract-review` label on the PR.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. Open question 1 (5988341325), `FileSystemRepository` provenance for pre-change log entries, recommended A. Accepted as A. The FS repository is attached as an event source only (`packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts:520-539`); the manager only calls `repo.watch({})` on it (`metadata-manager.ts:3018-3020`); `getRepository()` (`:2991`) has no caller in `packages/*/src`; no `.put(` on a repository exists outside the three repository packages. The residue is stated in the fs changeset (line 9). The version-pinned `get` answering null for an old token (`metadata-fs/src/repository.ts:264`) is the same residue with the same reach.
2. Open question 2 (5988341325), inline locale maps, recommended A. Accepted as A. `i18n-label-resolver.ts:44` and `:47` describe limbs 3 and 6 as a key-insertion-order tie-break mirrored from objectui's `pickLocalized`, not an authoring contract. The "declaration order is load-bearing" remark at `i18n.zod.ts:69-73` is about module load order under `OS_EAGER_SCHEMAS`, not about map keys. The table's own rule refuses a row inferred from renderer behaviour (`canonicalize.ts:89-91`). No row is owed.
3. Patch-1 open question (5988409457), `revertCommit` hands a stored manifest plural to `put`, recommended A for this PR and B as its own card. Accepted. Verified at `protocol.ts:23840` (guard) and `:23876` (ref from the stored type) and `:24058` (restore). #21821 exists, is open, graded `priority:p3`, labelled `pm:on-hold`, and names option B. The PR body's Acceptance notes carry the residue. Option C is rightly refused.
4. Deviation (5988341325): the full `metadata-protocol` suite ran before the last merge. Moot on this head: Test Core 1 to 6 are `success` here.
5. Deviation (5988341325): three PR-context gates exited 2 before the PR existed. Moot: "The card this PR closes must claim this branch", "Part-of PR must not also close its card", "No other open PR may claim the same issue" and "No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path" are `success` on the head.
6. Deviation (5988409457): a local probe commit made with hooks disabled was reset and never pushed. The branch holds seven commits from `e647cfcafe` to `046c425d62`; none is that commit.
7. Out-of-scope finding (5988341325), `DatabaseLoader`'s second checksum vocabulary, "carrier: none". The conclusion holds; its premise does not. `MetadataManager.register` is called from `packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts:1199`, `:1211`, `:1256` and `:1374`, so "no caller in `packages/*/src`" is wrong. `register` persists through every writable `datasource:` loader (`metadata-manager.ts:802-817`), and `DatabaseLoader.save` skips on an equal key-sorted bare-hex checksum (`database-loader.ts:1404-1414`, `metadata-history-utils.ts:18-30`). That door is boot-time artifact priming, not the designer's save-and-publish, which goes through `protocol.ts` to `SysMetadataRepository` and is pinned on the real stack by the dogfood file. So the card's door is closed. Escalated, not blocking: the same defect class on that loader deserves its own card, and the report's "no caller" sentence should not be repeated.
8. Out-of-scope finding (5988341325), `packages/objectql/scripts/dry-run-hash-compat.ts` hashes type-blind and its `checksum_drift` arm will fire on new stamps. Accepted as not blocking: it is the PR-10d.1 offline audit (`dry-run-hash-compat.ts:1-29`), not shipped (`objectql/package.json:63-66`, `files` is `dist` only). Escalated: a one-line follow-up (pass `row.type`) or a card, so the probe does not report false drift.
9. Out-of-scope finding (5988341325), I18nLabel maps: answered under item 2.
10. Acceptance note (PR body): a reorder into sorted order over a legacy row writes a `checksum` equal to its `previous_checksum`, so `getByHash` can find either history row. Verified: `getByHash` is a `findOne` by checksum (`sys-metadata-repository.ts:488-495`); `object` is `executionPinned: false` (`spec/src/kernel/metadata-plugin.zod.ts:726`); rollback resolves by the numeric history `version`, not by hash (`:1033`, `:1063`); and no production code in `packages/*/src` calls `getByHash`. Accepted. The one residue is the sentence at `types.ts:94-95` (item ① above).
11. Acceptance note (PR body): `FileSystemRepository` takes the type from the directory name verbatim. Accepted under item 1 (no production writer).
12. Owed docs item (5988464990), done per 5988540414: `metadata-lifecycle.mdx:149` now matches the code, and Build Docs and Check Documentation Links are `success` on the head. The Docs Drift Check (5988314939) named only that page, and it also said `packages/metadata-core/src/repository.ts` yielded no anchor; I read that file's change myself (`repository.ts:24-29`, the invariant text) and found no page it falsifies.
13. Main moved (5988540414): the head does not merge `ba57588665`. CI judged the merge of this head into `ba57588665` (5988314939), so the green gates cover the newer tree. `origin/main` has since moved again; the merge-base is still the PR's base sha, and the diff is clean against it.
14. The claim (5987515805) predicted `Clause-②: no` and said a contract review becomes owed if `packages/spec/src/**` is edited. No spec file is edited; the review is owed instead by the `yes` the diff produced, which the dev declared (5988464990).
